about: Single source of the physical constants used by the browser (assets/data/physical-constants.js), the Netlify Functions (netlify/lib/physical-constants.mjs) and the tests. Generated by tools/build-physical-constants.mjs; edit this file, then run the generator.

N_A.source: SI, 2019 redefinition: exact (BIPM, The International System of Units, 9th ed., 2019; CODATA 2018)

k_B.source: SI, 2019 redefinition: exact (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed.; CODATA 2018)

e.source: SI, 2019 redefinition: exact (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed.; CODATA 2018)

h.source: SI, 2019 redefinition: exact (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed.; CODATA 2018)

c.source: SI definition of the metre: exact (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed.)

R.source: R = N_A·k_B, exact since the 2019 SI (CODATA 2018: 8.314 462 618… J·mol⁻¹·K⁻¹)

F.source: F = N_A·e, exact since the 2019 SI (CODATA 2018: 96 485.332 12… C·mol⁻¹)

T0.source: Definition of the degree Celsius: t/°C = T/K − 273.15 (BIPM SI Brochure, 9th ed.)

atm.source: Definition: 1 atm = 101 325 Pa (NIST SP 811, 2008, appendix B.8)

bar.source: Definition: 1 bar = 10⁵ Pa (NIST SP 811, 2008, appendix B.8)

torr.source: Definition: 1 Torr = (101 325 / 760) Pa (NIST SP 811, 2008, appendix B.8)

mmHg.source: Conventional: ρ(Hg) = 13 595.1 kg·m⁻³ and g_n = 9.806 65 m·s⁻² over 1 mm = 133.322 387 415 Pa (NIST SP 811, 2008, appendix B.8 lists 1.333 224 E+02 Pa)

Kw25.source: Kw ≈ 1.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ at 25 °C (pKw ≈ 14.00; CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics), the value the pH calculator uses
